_README: SANITIZED ILLUSTRATION — NOT A DROP-IN IMPORT.
This is a genericized version of a production n8n workflow, published as a portfolio code sample.
All credentials, internal hostnames, schema names, table/column names, and client identifiers
have been removed or replaced with neutral placeholders. The control flow and SQL/JS logic are
faithful to the original pattern; the names are not. Do not expect it to run as-is.
Pattern: the core catalogue-insertion job. Runs four idempotent SQL steps in sequence on a
schedule: clean brand text -> dedupe staging & upsert products (validated against a
self-referencing taxonomy table) -> promote EAN rows to variants with size normalisation ->
queue manufacturer-part-number items for variant discovery -> clean up backlog/staging.
Every step uses ON CONFLICT so re-running is always safe.
name: catalogue-creation-automatic-addition (sanitized)

parameters.query:
-- Pre-step: strip quoting/escape characters from brand so match keys stay clean.
UPDATE staging_products
SET brand = REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(brand, $$['"]$$, '-', 'g'), $$[;\\%]$$, '', 'g')
WHERE brand ~ $$['";\\%]$$;

nodes.name: Pre: clean brand text
nodes.notes: credentials intentionally omitted in this sanitized sample

parameters.query:
-- Step 1: dedupe staging, upsert into products (validated against the taxonomy),
--         and seed descriptions. Idempotent via ON CONFLICT.
BEGIN;

WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT ctid, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY brand, match_key ORDER BY ctid) AS rn
    FROM staging_products
)
DELETE FROM staging_products
WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid FROM ranked WHERE rn > 1);

INSERT INTO products (
    category_level_1, category_level_2, category_level_3, use_case,
    brand, match_key, product_name, colour, rrp, updated_at, attributes, model_name
)
SELECT
    sp.category_level_1, c2.name AS category_level_2, sp.category_level_3, sp.use_case,
    sp.brand, sp.match_key,
    REPLACE(sp.product_name, sp.brand || ' ', '') AS product_name,  -- strip leading brand
    LOWER(sp.colour), sp.rrp, NOW(), sp.attributes, sp.model_name
FROM staging_products sp
INNER JOIN category_reference c1
    ON c1.name = sp.category_level_1 AND c1.category_level = 'category_level_1'
LEFT JOIN category_reference c2
    ON c2.name = sp.category_level_2 AND c2.category_level = 'category_level_2'
    AND c1.id = c2.parent_category_id   -- self-referencing taxonomy hierarchy
WHERE sp.description IS NOT NULL AND sp.description <> '' AND c2.name IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (brand, match_key) DO UPDATE SET
    category_level_1 = EXCLUDED.category_level_1,
    category_level_2 = EXCLUDED.category_level_2,
    category_level_3 = EXCLUDED.category_level_3,
    use_case         = EXCLUDED.use_case,
    product_name     = EXCLUDED.product_name,
    colour           = EXCLUDED.colour,
    rrp              = EXCLUDED.rrp,
    attributes       = products.attributes || EXCLUDED.attributes;  -- merge JSON attrs

INSERT INTO product_descriptions (product_id, description_text)
SELECT p.id, sp.description
FROM staging_products sp
INNER JOIN products p ON sp.match_key = p.match_key AND p.brand = sp.brand
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM product_descriptions d WHERE d.product_id = p.id)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

COMMIT;

parameters.query:
-- Step 2: promote EAN-keyed rows into variants, normalise size strings, refresh counts.
BEGIN;

WITH valid_ean AS (
    SELECT brand, match_key, (match_key ~ '^\d{13}$') AS is_valid_ean
    FROM staging_products
    WHERE is_match_key_mpn = FALSE
)
INSERT INTO staging_variants (brand, match_key, ean, created_at)
SELECT brand, match_key, match_key AS ean, NOW()
FROM valid_ean
WHERE is_valid_ean
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products p WHERE p.match_key = valid_ean.match_key)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM staging_variants sv WHERE sv.ean = valid_ean.match_key)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

WITH size_normalised AS (
    SELECT brand, match_key, ean,
        REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(
            size,'.00',''),'.50',' 1/2'),'.5',' 1/2'),'.33',' 1/3'),'.3',' 1/3'),'.67',' 2/3'),'.6',' 2/3') AS final_size
    FROM staging_variants
)
INSERT INTO variants (product_id, ean, size)
SELECT p.id, sn.ean, sn.final_size
FROM products p
INNER JOIN size_normalised sn ON p.brand = sn.brand AND p.match_key = sn.match_key
ON CONFLICT (ean) DO NOTHING;

UPDATE products p
SET variant_count = sq.variant_count
FROM (
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS variant_count
    FROM variants
    WHERE created_at >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 week'
    GROUP BY product_id
) sq
WHERE p.id = sq.product_id;

TRUNCATE staging_variants;
COMMIT;

parameters.query:
-- Step 3: items that arrived as a manufacturer part number have no variants yet.
--         Queue them for downstream variant/EAN discovery.
INSERT INTO enrichment_backlog (product_id, is_match_key_mpn, priority, process, created_at)
SELECT p.id, TRUE, 100, 'investigate_mpn', NOW()
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN variants v ON p.id = v.product_id
WHERE DATE(p.created_at) = CURRENT_DATE
  AND v.id IS NULL
  AND category_level_2 IN ('clothing','footwear','sports-shoes','sports-clothing')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
